documents.unit: University Policy Register (Office of General Counsel / Provost)
documents.title: 3342-3-01.8 Administrative policy regarding student cheating and plagiarism
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); revised to add generative AI
documents.stance_why: GAI is treated as cheating on exams ("except as expressly permitted by the instructor") and on assigned coursework ("except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment"), so AI is banned unless the instructor explicitly permits it. It sets a restrictive default rather than only delegating, and offers no tiers.
documents.summary: Kent State's administrative policy on student cheating and plagiarism, revised to add generative AI. GAI is defined, barred on exams and coursework unless the instructor expressly permits it, and added to the cheating and plagiarism definitions, with the general sanction, appeal and hearing procedures applying.

units.why: The purpose clause says academic work follows "standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges", so standards are set below the university level; this is a general principle placing authority with instructors and units, which fits P04 (who decides) better than P56, since it is not an AI-specific framework.
units.anchor: standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges
units.frag_start: Students enrolled in the university
units.policy: Students perform their academic work according to standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges.

units.why: States that "cheating and plagiarism constitute fraudulent misrepresentation for which no credit can be given" and sanctions "will be applied"; it is the general rationale for treating improper work (which includes GAI misuse) as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: cheating and plagiarism constitute fraudulent misrepresentation for which no credit can be given
units.frag_start: Students enrolled in the university

units.why: Defines cheating to include "content generated by internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs (GAI), in examinations, tests and quizzes" unless the instructor permits it; this is an exam ban with an instructor-permission exception, so P22 (exam ban) rather than P06 (fallback), and it also classifies it as cheating.
units.anchor: content generated by internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs (GAI), in examinations, tests and quizzes
units.frag_start: Using notes, textbooks or other information, or content
units.policy: Using content generated by internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs (GAI) in examinations, tests and quizzes is cheating, except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz.

units.why: The exception "except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz" lets each instructor decide whether GAI is allowed on exams, so P04 (instructor sets the rule) is assigned; the exam ban itself is coded separately under P22.
units.anchor: except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz
units.frag_start: Using notes, textbooks or other information, or content
units.policy: The instructor may expressly permit GAI use in an examination, test or quiz in the syllabus or in the examination, test or quiz itself.

units.why: "Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction of assigned coursework" is defined as cheating unless the instructor expressly permits it, i.e. students may not have AI produce the work they submit: P19, not P22 because it concerns coursework not exams.
units.anchor: Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction of assigned coursework
units.frag_start: Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction
units.policy: Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction of assigned coursework is cheating, except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment.

units.why: The clause "except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment" is a default-prohibited rule with permission only if explicitly given, i.e. the fallback when a syllabus is silent; P06 fits better than P04 because it fixes what applies without permission.
units.anchor: except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment
units.frag_start: Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction
units.policy: GAI use to generate content for assigned coursework is allowed only where the instructor expressly permits it in the syllabus or applicable assignment.

units.why: Cheating includes "Presenting data or other material gathered by another person, group, or by GAI, as one's own", a rule against passing off AI-gathered material as one's own; P29 (submitted work must be own) fits since it targets presentation as own work, not generation.
units.anchor: gathered by another person, group, or by GAI, as one's own
units.frag_start: Presenting data or other material gathered
units.policy: Presenting data or other material gathered by GAI as one's own is cheating.

units.why: Cheating includes "Having another person, or GAI, take one's place for any academic performance without the specific knowledge and permission of the instructor"; AI substituting for the student is forbidden unless the instructor knowingly permits, which is a ban on AI producing the submitted performance, P19.
units.anchor: Having another person, or GAI, take one's place for any academic performance
units.frag_start: Having another person, or GAI
units.policy: Having GAI take one's place for any academic performance without the specific knowledge and permission of the instructor is cheating.

units.why: Plagiarize is defined as presenting as one's own "the ideas or words of another (e.g. person, persons, or GAI)", which puts GAI in the same category as human sources, so P45 (treat AI like a human source under existing rules).
units.anchor: the ideas or words of another (e.g. person, persons, or GAI)
units.frag_start: "Plagiarize" means to take and present
units.frag_end: proper credit to the source of the ideas, words, or works
units.policy: Presenting as one's own a material portion of the ideas or words of another, including GAI, is plagiarism.

units.why: The plagiarism definition covers presenting work "without full and proper credit to the source", which for GAI sources requires crediting the AI; this is an attribution requirement, P24, though it is only implicit for AI.
units.anchor: without full and proper credit to the source of the ideas, words, or works
units.frag_start: or to present as one's own an idea
units.policy: Presenting as one's own an idea or work derived from an existing source without full and proper credit to the source is plagiarism.

units.why: The definition of GAI as "internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs that make use of large language model algorithms" fixes what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs that make use of large language model algorithms
units.frag_start: "Generative artificial intelligence program (GAI)" means any

units.why: The carve-out says "AI used for auto-complete, minor text-predictions, and/or grammar/spelling/punctuation suggestions" is "not considered GAI", scoping the policy to exclude editor and word-processor assistance; P07 covers AI built into tools but this excludes it, and scope definition is the fit, so P61 with unit_stance permit.
units.anchor: is not considered GAI
units.frag_start: AI used for auto-complete, minor text-predictions
units.policy: AI used for auto-complete, minor text-predictions, and/or grammar/spelling/punctuation suggestions, commonly found in most word-processing applications, is not considered GAI.

units.why: Says the university "affirms that acts of cheating and plagiarism by students constitute a subversion of the goals of the institution"; a statement of purpose for the integrity policy (including its GAI provisions), so P56.
units.anchor: acts of cheating and plagiarism by students constitute a subversion of the goals
units.frag_start: In providing this policy, the university affirms

units.why: States the policy "applies to all students of the university, graduate and undergraduate, full or part-time", setting scope that includes the GAI provisions; scope statement, P61.
units.anchor: applies to all students of the university, graduate and undergraduate, full or part-time
units.frag_start: This policy applies to all students of the university

units.why: Instructors may "Assign a grade of 'F' or zero for the project, test, paper, examination or other work" or fail the course; these are concrete penalties available for cheating, which includes GAI misuse, so P37.
units.anchor: Assign a grade of "F" or zero for the project, test, paper, examination
units.frag_start: Assign a grade of "F" or zero

units.why: The instructor may assign a course "F", an additional stated coursework sanction; kept separate from the zero/F-on-work unit as a different penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Assign a grade of "F" for the course in which the cheating
units.frag_start: Assign a grade of "F" for the course

units.why: Degree-level sanctions such as "Recommendation for revocation of a degree" are listed for cheating that compromises a degree; stated penalties escalating by severity, P37.
units.anchor: Recommendation for revocation of a degree
units.frag_start: Recommendation for revocation of a degree
units.frag_end: Recommendation for revocation of a degree

units.why: The hearing panel may impose "Disciplinary probation", suspension or dismissal; escalating stated penalties for proven misconduct, P37.
units.anchor: This sanction is one of involuntary separation of the student from the university
units.frag_start: Disciplinary dismissal. This sanction is one

units.why: Instructors must "Inform the student as soon as is practical of the belief that an act of cheating or plagiarism has occurred", a duty to talk to the student before sanctioning, which is P57.
units.anchor: Inform the student as soon as is practical of the belief that an act
units.frag_start: Inform the student as soon as is practical

units.why: The instructor must "Provide the student an opportunity to explain orally, in writing, or both", a right to respond to allegations, so P64 (not P57, which is about gathering context before escalating).
units.anchor: Provide the student an opportunity to explain orally, in writing, or both
units.frag_start: Provide the student an opportunity to explain
units.frag_end: evaluation of the facts is erroneous

units.why: The instructor acts where "it is more probable than not" that cheating occurred, setting an evidentiary standard for misconduct including GAI; it fits P36 (handled by integrity process) best.
units.anchor: it is more probable than not that a student
units.frag_start: In the event that an instructor determines that
units.frag_end: act of cheating, plagiarism or cooperation in either
units.policy: An instructor who determines that it is more probable than not that a student has presented work involving cheating, plagiarism or cooperation in either follows the stated procedure.

units.why: Instructors "shall keep the evidence of cheating or plagiarism in a secure place" and provide it on request, a procedural evidence rule for integrity cases; P36 as the closest enforcement type.
units.anchor: keep the evidence of cheating or plagiarism in a secure place
units.frag_start: The instructor shall keep the evidence
units.policy: The instructor keeps the evidence of cheating or plagiarism in a secure place and provides it upon request to the department chair, dean, or academic hearing panel, and to the student at the student's expense.

units.why: The appeals provision gives students a right to appeal "within fifteen working days" to the academic hearing panel; a fairness safeguard in integrity cases, P64.
units.anchor: by the student within fifteen working days
units.frag_start: An appeal of a sanction imposed

units.why: Hearing rules say the "burden of establishing by a preponderance of the evidence" is on the accuser and the student "may make a statement" and examine evidence; fairness for accused students, P64.
units.anchor: The burden of establishing by a preponderance of the evidence that cheating
units.frag_start: The burden of establishing by a preponderance

units.why: Both parties "have the right to hear all testimony and examine all evidence", a procedural right of the accused; P64.
units.anchor: Both have the right to hear all testimony and examine all evidence
units.frag_start: Both have the right to hear

units.why: Plagiarism school offers a "remedial, private session" to mitigate sanctions for unintentional plagiarism for students not previously sanctioned; mitigation in return for remediation is closest to P38 (reduced consequences), though it is not a self-report window.
units.anchor: attend a remedial, private session administered by university libraries
units.frag_start: the instructor may request that the student attend
units.policy: For less severe cases of plagiarism, the instructor may request that the student attend a remedial, private session administered by university libraries regarding acceptable ways to document research.

units.why: Plagiarism school "will only be offered to students not previously sanctioned for plagiarism", limiting the mitigation; the same P38 mechanism with an eligibility condition.
units.anchor: Plagiarism school will only be offered to students not previously sanctioned for plagiarism
units.frag_start: Plagiarism school will only be offered

units.why: The academic hearing panel is appointed by the provost with faculty and student members and decides cases; an institutional process for adjudicating misconduct including GAI, P36.
units.anchor: The panel shall be appointed by the provost
units.frag_start: Composition. The panel shall be appointed

units.why: "Annual training will be offered" for panel members; a procedural support obligation on administrators not about AI use and fitting no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Annual training will be offered
units.frag_start: Annual training will be offered
units.uncovered_note: Training of academic hearing panel members for integrity cases; procedural support, not about AI use.

units.why: Panel members who are current instructors of the accused or share affiliation "are not eligible to sit", an impartiality safeguard in integrity cases, P64.
units.anchor: are not eligible to sit on the AHP hearing committee
units.frag_start: Faculty who are current instructors of the accused student

units.why: Hearings are "closed to the public and are recorded", a record-keeping and confidentiality rule for integrity cases; closest is P64 transparency and fairness.
units.anchor: All AHP hearings are closed to the public and are recorded
units.frag_start: All AHP hearings are closed to the public

units.why: Students, faculty and deans "may appeal the decisions of the hearing board" to the provost, one final appeal on stated grounds; P64.
units.anchor: may appeal the decisions of the hearing board or officers to the provost
units.frag_start: Students, faculty, and deans may appeal
units.frag_end: No additional appeal will be heard

units.why: The policy states it is intended "to provide safeguards for any student suspected of cheating or plagiarism", an explicit fairness commitment, P64.
units.anchor: to provide safeguards for any student suspected of cheating or plagiarism
units.frag_start: It is the intent of this policy to provide appropriate sanctions

notes: Kent State CS department page https://www.kent.edu/cs/academic-dishonesty (fetched as v2-kent-state-cs-dishonesty.txt) is a policy on collaboration in programming assignments and has no AI or GAI text, so it was not collected. Computing therefore counts as none-found, though the page does state the department's cooperation rules. The Kent news item about the policy revision (kent.edu/today/news/adding-ai-cheating-and-plagiarism-policy) is a news article and was not collected. The CTL faculty AI pages (kent.edu/ai/faculty) return 'Access denied'; search snippets say the CTL offers model syllabus language for AI prohibited / permitted / integrated, but the text was not retrieved.
